config.title: Test useFetch

intro.title: Test useFetch
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a test for a custom React hook called `useFetch` that fetches data from an API. You'll learn how to write unit tests using React Testing Library and Jest to verify that the hook correctly handles loading states, successful data returns, and error scenarios. The core programming concept involves mocking HTTP requests with tools like `jest.mock` or `fetch.mock` to simulate different API responses without making real network calls. You'll work with React hooks, asynchronous testing patterns, and assertion methods to ensure your custom hook behaves as expected under various conditions.
intro.usecase: Testing custom hooks like useFetch is a critical skill for ensuring data reliability in production React applications. Developers must verify that components fetching user profiles, dashboard metrics, or product listings handle loading, error, and success states correctly. For example, in an e-commerce admin panel, robust tests for a useFetch hook powering order history or inventory data prevent UI crashes and provide a seamless user experience. This practice ensures your application remains stable and responsive when integrating with real APIs.

objectives: Implement a test suite for a custom React hook using React Testing Library.
Construct mock HTTP responses to simulate different API behaviors in tests.
Apply asynchronous testing utilities to verify loading, success, and error states.
Configure test scenarios to validate the hook's data fetching and state updates.
Integrate cleanup procedures to reset mocks and ensure test isolation.
Render a test component that utilizes the custom hook within a testing environment.

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.

// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added to the top of the file.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState.

steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Initialize state for loading status
steps.instruction: Inside your TestComponent function component, call useState to create a loading state variable and setter, initialized to true.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The syntax is: const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a loading state variable initialized to true, ready to track loading status.
successCriteria: TestComponent contains a useState call that creates a loading state variable and setter, initialized to true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're calling useState inside TestComponent with the initial value set to true.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using useState correctly inside TestComponent. The syntax should be: const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);

steps.title: Initialize state for fetched data
steps.instruction: Inside your TestComponent, call useState again to create a state variable named 'data' and its setter, initialized to null.
steps.hint: Use the same useState pattern you used for loading, but name the variable 'data' and set its initial value to null.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state for storing user info
const [user, setUser] = useState(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have two state variables: loading (boolean) and data (null initially).
successCriteria: A state variable named 'data' is declared with useState, initialized to null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to declare a variable named 'data' with an initial value of null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside TestComponent, use useState to create a state variable called 'data' and set its initial value to null.

steps.title: Define the fetchData handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the TestComponent function, define an async function named fetchData that will fetch data from a test API URL.
steps.hint: Create an async function using the async keyword before the function definition. You can use a placeholder URL like 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos/1' for testing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TestComponent should now contain an async fetchData function definition, ready to implement the fetch logic in later steps.
successCriteria: An async function named fetchData is defined inside TestComponent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function is async and named exactly fetchData. Check that it's defined inside the TestComponent function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetchData function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create an async function named fetchData inside the TestComponent.

steps.title: Implement fetchData to update state
steps.instruction: Inside the fetchData function, implement the fetch logic: set loading to true, fetch data from 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos/1', parse the JSON response, set the data state with the result, and set loading to false.
steps.hint: Use the fetch API with the URL, handle the promise chain with .then() and .catch(), and call the state setters at the appropriate times.
steps.expectedOutcome: The fetchData function is fully implemented with the fetch call and state updates.
successCriteria: fetchData sets loading to true, fetches from the URL, parses JSON, sets data with the result, and sets loading to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're setting loading to true at the start, fetching the URL, parsing JSON, updating data, and setting loading to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetchData function is not implemented as required. Review the steps: set loading true, fetch, parse JSON, update data, set loading false.

steps.instruction: In your component's JSX, add a button element with the text 'Fetch Data' inside it.
steps.hint: Add a <button> tag with 'Fetch Data' as its content before the return statement's null.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component should return a button with the text 'Fetch Data'.
successCriteria: A <button> element with the text 'Fetch Data' is present in the JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a <button> element with the exact text 'Fetch Data'.

steps.title: Display loading state in JSX
steps.instruction: In the return statement of your component, add a conditional that shows a paragraph with the text 'Loading...' when the loading state is true.
steps.hint: You can use a ternary operator or logical AND (&&) to conditionally render the paragraph based on the loading state value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display 'Loading...' text when the loading state is true, and nothing when it's false.
successCriteria: A paragraph element with 'Loading...' text is conditionally rendered based on the loading state value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the paragraph only appears when loading is true. Check your conditional syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The loading state isn't being displayed conditionally. Remember to use the loading state variable in your JSX with a conditional operator.

steps.title: Display fetched data when available
steps.instruction: In your component's JSX, after the loading check, add a conditional statement to display the data state value when it's not null.
steps.hint: You can use a logical AND (&&) operator to conditionally render JSX when data exists.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will show fetched data when the data state contains a value.
successCriteria: The JSX includes a conditional statement that renders the data value when data is not null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're checking if data exists and rendering it appropriately.
steps.feedbackWrong: The data isn't being displayed conditionally. Check if you're using the correct state variable and conditional logic.
